title: A BATS formation-only box needs extra inflow when measured density-layer thickness is imposed
abstract: We test a finite-volume renewal model for the BATS 26.4-26.6 density layer. We use published annual thickness, AOU and three basin formation histories. Calibration uses only 1989-1998 means and an assumed tracer-based oxygen-use rate. No changes are fitted. For 1999-2022, measured thickness changes AOU error little: RMSE goes from 7.08 to 6.58 umol/kg with ERA5, 7.26 to 7.35 with NCEP R1, and 10.15 to 10.10 with R2. Each conditional paired error interval includes zero. The mapped formation inflow and measured expansion require negative outflow in 2, 3 and 1 of 24 intervals. We derive a joint water and deficit bound with nonnegative source AOU. Under annual linear-state assumptions, the bound needs at least 212, 202 and 171 m of added cumulative inflow per unit area. Extra inflow with layer AOU preserves the concentration curve; young inflow changes it. Thus observed volume alone does not fix the oxygen effect. These are conditional local model requirements, not measured transports or a rejection of ventilation. Annual interpolation, one site, steady early calibration, unknown boundary properties and fixed oxygen use limit the result.

display.caption: Measured thickness gives little AOU error gain and needs extra inflow to close the local water budget. Main calibration and 1999-2022 test; grey region uses post-2022 infill.
